name: bpmsoft-intellisense
description: Autocomplete and navigation for BPMSoft AMD modules in Pkg

commands.title: Local History: найти запись для восстановления…

bpmsoft.pkgGlob.description: Glob for package schema JS files to index

bpmsoft.platformUiGlob.description: Glob for platform Ext UI classes (override/extend targets like BPMSoft.controls.Grid)

bpmsoft.enablePlatformStubs.description: Include static BPMSoft.* platform stubs in completions

bpmsoft.preferIndexedCompletions.description: Disable JS word/name history suggestions in workspace so indexed BPMSoft completions rank first

bpmsoft.styleDiagnostics.description: Check style in editable JS and C# files. JS skips Autogenerated / UI / conf. C# also checks Autogenerated/Src (opened by C# Dev Kit). JS: K&R, var/const, eqeqeq, unused locals and schema members, switch, curly braces, camelCase methods/locals. C#: Allman braces, if/switch, naming conventions.

bpmsoft.csharpXmlDocDiagnostics.description: Warn when a public/protected C# method or property has no /// XML-doc comment above it. Off by default: existing codebases rarely have full XML-doc coverage, so this would be noisy until you opt in.

bpmsoft.trailingCommentDiagnostics.description: Warn when a // comment (JS or C#) sits at the end of a code line instead of on its own line above, per the JS/C# style guides. Disable if this is too noisy on an existing codebase that hasn't followed the convention.

bpmsoft.selectAllColumnsHint.description: Info-level hint on AddAllSchemaColumns()/FetchFromDB() without an explicit column list (C#) and esq.allColumns = true (JS): double-check you actually need every column. Silence a specific call site with a // bpmsoft-ignore: select-all-columns comment on the line above, or use the 'Not a problem' quick fix.

bpmsoft.formatting.enabled.description: Register BPMSoft's Format Document providers for JS/C#/SQL-script files (Prettier + our own style fixes for JS; brace/spacing/blank-line auto-fixes for C#; sql-formatter for Pkg/*/SqlScripts/*.sql). Works with the standard Format Document command / Shift+Alt+F / editor.formatOnSave. Turn off if you'd rather use another formatter for these languages.

bpmsoft.namingDiagnostics.description: Check client schema / C# schema / SQL script names against naming-guidelines.md (type-appropriate suffix, e.g. Section/SectionV2, Page/PageV2, Detail/DetailV2, and — only where the platform gives an unambiguous marker — Service/EventListener for C#). Surfaced both as squiggles on open descriptor.json/.cs files and in the 'BPMSoft: Naming Issues' view.

bpmsoft.namingPrefixes.description: Comma-separated package/schema name prefixes to require (e.g. "Nau" or "Nau,Go" for multiple streams). Empty (default) disables the prefix check — there's no one universal prefix to assume.

bpmsoft.gitFlowDiagnostics.description: Check the current git branch against the team's Git Flow model (main/develop/sprint/x.x.x/release/x.x.x/feature/bugfix) and show violations in the status bar. Covers: branch name pattern, main never carrying commits absent from develop, and (see bpmsoft.gitFlow.checkBranchParent) feature/bugfix branched from the right parent. Can't check step *order* — that's not recoverable from git history alone.

bpmsoft.gitFlow.checkBranchParent.description: Heuristically check that feature/* was branched from a sprint/* branch and bugfix/* from a release/* branch, not straight off develop/main — based on merge-base analysis of git history, so it can false-positive on a branch that was created correctly but never rebased/updated from its parent. Turn off if it's too noisy; the other bpmsoft.gitFlowDiagnostics checks are unaffected.

bpmsoft.packageOwnershipDiagnostics.description: Check the active file's package against bpmsoft.namingPrefixes and bpmsoft.expectedMaintainers (stand-ins for the SchemaNamePrefix/Maintainer system settings — no DB connection to read those directly), reading each package's own descriptor.json. Violations show in the status bar.

bpmsoft.currentPackage.description: Reference value for the package you're currently working in — stand-in for the CurrentPackageId system setting. Shown in the 'Package Settings' view; not yet enforced as a check (see bpmsoft.packageOwnershipDiagnostics for what actually is).

bpmsoft.expectedMaintainers.description: Comma-separated Maintainer value(s) your team's packages should have (e.g. "YandexGo") — stand-in for the Maintainer system setting. Empty (default) disables the maintainer check.

bpmsoft.entityNamingDiagnostics.description: Check EntitySchemaManager objects (naming-guidelines.md §2 'Объекты') against their own descriptor.json/metadata.json/Resources: object Code (PascalCase, prefix, singular, no Tbl/Entity/Field affix), ru-RU/en-US Title coverage, custom column Code (prefix, boolean Is/Has/Can prefix, date suffix, no redundant lookup 'Id' suffix, no redundant repetition of the owning entity's name), and cross-package Code uniqueness (aware of the substitution mechanism — the same Code across packages via ExtendParent is expected, not a collision).

bpmsoft.entityNaming.checkSingularName.description: Part of bpmsoft.entityNamingDiagnostics: flag an object Code that looks plural. Kept as its own toggle — English has no reliable syntactic plural rule without a dictionary, so this heuristic (ends in 's', not 'ss'/'us'/'is') is noisier than the other checks.

bpmsoft.entityNaming.singularExceptions.description: Comma-separated object Codes that are legitimately plural by meaning, exempt from bpmsoft.entityNaming.checkSingularName.

bpmsoft.entityNaming.dateSuffixes.description: Comma-separated acceptable suffixes for DATE/DATE_TIME/TIME column names (e.g. CreatedOn/ModifiedOn → "On", StartDate → "Date").

bpmsoft.entityNaming.booleanPrefixes.description: Comma-separated acceptable verb/assertion prefixes for BOOLEAN column names (e.g. IsActive, HasAttachment, CanEdit).

bpmsoft.sqlTempScriptMaxAgeDays.description: naming-guidelines.md §6: a _Temp SQL script should be removed from the package after its one-time run on target environments. This extension can't know what's actually been deployed, so it's a nudge, not a hard check — a _Temp script older than this many days (by its git add date) gets flagged as 'possibly forgotten'. 0 disables it.
